meta.title: Sample Receipt, Identification, and Labelling Procedure

sections.purpose: To establish a standardized procedure for receiving, uniquely identifying, labelling, and tracking all samples submitted to the pharmacy laboratory for analysis, ensuring chain of custody, traceability, and prevention of sample mix-up or confusion.
sections.scope: Applicable to all pharmacy laboratory departments that receive samples for analysis — including drug substance samples, formulated product samples, crude drug samples, environmental samples, and water quality samples.
procedure: Receive the sample from the submitter along with a completed Sample Submission Form containing: sample name, batch/lot number, quantity, storage conditions, tests required, date of collection/manufacture, and submitter's name and contact.

Inspect the sample on receipt: verify the physical condition (container integrity, no leakage, no tampering), label information matches the submission form, and quantity is adequate for all specified tests.
Reject and return any sample that arrives in a damaged container, is inadequately labelled, or has a discrepancy with the submission form — document the reason for rejection.
Assign a unique Laboratory Sample Number (LSN) to every accepted sample: format — DEPT/YEAR/SEQUENTIAL (e.g., PA/2026/0047).
Record the sample in the Sample Receipt Register: LSN, date received, sample name, batch number, submitter name, tests requested, quantity received, and storage location assigned.
Apply a laboratory sample label to every container: LSN, sample name, batch/lot number, date received, storage condition, test(s) required, and assigned analyst.
Do not remove the original manufacturer/supplier label from the sample container — the laboratory label is applied in addition to, not instead of, the original label.

Assign the sample to the designated storage location based on its required storage condition: room temperature (15–25°C), refrigerator (2–8°C), or freezer (−20°C); record location in the Sample Receipt Register.
Assign the sample to the appropriate analyst and note the assignment date in the register.
The analyst acknowledges receipt of the sample by signing the register.
Track the sample through all analysis stages: sample login → analysis → reporting → archival/disposal.

After completion of analysis, retain a portion of the sample (retain sample) in a sealed, labelled container for a minimum of one year or per applicable specification — store in the designated retain sample area.
Document the final disposal of samples in the register when they are discarded as per the waste disposal SOP.
Review the Sample Receipt Register monthly for samples that have been pending analysis beyond the specified turnaround time.
precautions: Never analyse an unlabelled or inadequately identified sample — rejection and re-submission is mandatory.
Maintain unique laboratory sample numbers — duplicate numbers cause catastrophic sample mix-up and reporting errors.
Do not share sample containers between different tests unless the original container volume is adequate and sub-sampling is documented.
Handle all samples with appropriate PPE — assume all samples are potentially hazardous until the hazard class is confirmed.
Chain of custody must be unbroken — every transfer of a sample (from reception to analyst to storage) must be documented with date, time, and signature.
For legal, medico-legal, or dispute samples: maintain photographic evidence of sample condition on receipt; seal with tamper-evident tape; two-person verification of receipt.
Retain sample areas must be locked and access restricted to authorized personnel only.
